definitions.explanation: The group of people who oppose a specific plan, policy, or proposal, treated as one camp. Used of factions within an organization as well as of the public split over an issue.

examples.japanese: {反対派|はんたいは}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: The number of opponents is growing.

examples.japanese: {反対派|はんたいは}の{意見|いけん}にも{耳|みみ}を{傾|かたむ}けるべきだ。
examples.english: We should listen to the opponents' views as well.

examples.japanese: {計画|けいかく}は、{反対派|はんたいは}を{切|き}り{崩|くず}すかたちで{進|すす}められた。
examples.english: The plan was pushed forward by breaking down the opposition.

notes:
{反対|はんたい} (opposition) + the suffix 〜{派|は} (faction, camp). The suffix is productive: {推進派|すいしんは} (the pro-promotion camp), {慎重派|しんちょうは} (the cautious camp), {改革派|かいかくは} (the reformists).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {反対派|はんたいは}が{多|おお}い: opponents are numerous
- {反対派|はんたいは}を{説得|せっとく}する: to persuade the opposition
- {反対派|はんたいは}の{抵抗|ていこう}: resistance from the opposition

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {賛成派|さんせいは}: the camp in favor — the direct opposite
- {野党|やとう}: opposition party — a party out of power, not a stance on one issue
